papers.title: A Machine Learning Implementation to Predictive Maintenance and Monitoring of Industrial Compressors
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates the deployment of a machine learning approach integrated with IoT and multi-sensor data acquisition on an industrial air compressor unit. By utilizing temperature, pressure, and flow rate data processed through a Linear Regression model, the system achieves 98% accuracy in the Mean Squared Error metric, successfully predicting potential equipment failures and sending real-time warnings to operators.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Predictive Maintenance for Industrial Equipment Optimization
papers.summary: This research explores machine learning-based predictive maintenance for industrial equipment optimization. It covers sensor data preprocessing, feature engineering, anomaly detection for early failure detection, and predicting remaining useful life (RUL) to balance cost-effectiveness and equipment reliability in real-world industrial settings.

papers.title: Machine learning and IoT – Based predictive maintenance approach for industrial applications
papers.summary: This study presents a predictive maintenance system utilizing IoT-enabled devices and the AdaBoost machine learning algorithm to classify six different types of machine stops in real-time for knitting machines. The optimized model achieves 92% accuracy on the test set, demonstrating the capability to enable timely maintenance actions and improve productivity in the textile industry.

key_findings: Predictive maintenance models leveraging machine learning, IoT sensors, and multi-sensor data acquisition achieve high accuracies (such as 98% Mean Squared Error metrics for industrial compressor models and 92% accuracy for real-time machine stop classification in the textile industry).

Industrial predictive maintenance reduces unscheduled downtime, cuts maintenance expenses significantly across sectors like energy, manufacturing, and automotive, and enhances overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).

Modern frameworks increasingly emphasize digital twins, uncertainty quantification, remaining useful life (RUL) estimation, and scalable, explainable AI solutions to handle complex industrial environments and data integration challenges.
overall_summary: This selection of research papers published from 2023 onward covers advancements in industrial predictive maintenance, highlighting the integration of machine learning, Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, and digital twin architectures. The studies explore real-time monitoring, remaining useful life (RUL) estimation, and anomaly detection to transition industrial operations from reactive to proactive maintenance strategies, thereby minimizing unexpected downtime and maximizing equipment efficiency.
